intro: The full review of Leng Yentafo — Khon Kaen's Bib Gourmand pick — with everything you need to know before you go: prices, booking/queue, must-order dishes, and how to get there.
quickAnswerHtml: Leng Yentafo is a Bib Gourmand pick in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, located in Khon Kaen, in the in-town Thanon Klang Mueang area, for around under 100 THB/bowl. Mostly walk-in, queue at the door.

blocks.html:
Ask anyone in Khon Kaen which yentafo shop has been part of the city the longest, and "Leng Yentafo" comes up in nearly every answer. The shop has been open since 1984 — over 40 years now. It started with Khun Leng, a descendant of the Mae Sok Tiang family, ethnic Chinese, who decided to move from Yaowarat (Bangkok's Chinatown) to settle in Khon Kaen, bringing the secret recipe for pink yentafo broth with them. What began as a small noodle shop on Thanon Klang Mueang is today a legend that the MICHELIN Guide has awarded a Bib Gourmand, and it still holds a place in the 2026 edition. MICHELIN itself writes plainly that the shop's charm hasn't faded at all over more than forty years — for a noodle shop charging under 100 baht a bowl, that's a serious compliment.

The heart of the shop is an authentic Yaowarat-style yentafo, cooked the same way since the founding generation. The pink broth carries just the right amount of punch, the noodles that MICHELIN praised as especially soft and chewy, and what sets it apart from ordinary yentafo is what's in the bowl — fish balls and shrimp balls made fresh in-house, fish dumplings wrapped by hand one by one. One bite and you can tell it's not factory-made. Anyone who wants an extra kick should order the tom yum yentafo, its sour-spicy edge cutting nicely against the broth's sweetness. As for the side dish nearly every table orders, it's the deep-fried taro — crisp outside, soft inside, and unbelievably good paired with a hot bowl of noodles.

A charming detail: MICHELIN named Leng Yentafo one of the Best Breakfast Spots in Isan, because the shop opens at half past seven in the morning and stays open until midnight, so locals in Khon Kaen can eat here any time of day — from breakfast before work to a late bite after a night out. The location is right in the city center on Thanon Klang Mueang, easy to reach. Anyone visiting Khon Kaen who wants to understand why this city became a place where overseas Chinese settled down and left their culinary mark for later generations — this shop's pink bowl of yentafo is a real, edible answer. Since you're already in Khon Kaen, stop by and taste the legend. It costs less than a hundred baht, but you'll walk away with a story worth bringing home.

blocks.name: Leng Yentafo
blocks.descHtml:
Leng Yentafo sits on Thanon Klang Mueang, right in the center of Khon Kaen — easy to spot next to the 7-Eleven in front of Villa. Open daily 07:30–24:00 (some older sources list 07:00–03:00, so it's worth allowing some flexibility if you're heading there very late). Prices are easy on the wallet, under 100 THB a bowl. No reservation needed — just walk in and take a seat. Call 086-580-1259 if you have questions. One important thing to know: the shop accepts cash only, so bring small bills.

The best time to go is breakfast through lunch — MICHELIN named it one of the Best Breakfast Spots in Isan, and the queue is clearly shorter in the morning and midday than in the evening. The must-order dishes are the original-recipe yentafo, tom yum yentafo, house-made fish dumplings with fish balls, and deep-fried taro as a side. If the main branch is packed, there's a second branch near the Khon Kaen Hospital intersection as a backup option.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead at Leng Yentafo?
faq.a: No booking needed — it's a walk-in shop, just head in and take a seat. If you have questions, call 086-580-1259. One thing to know: the shop accepts cash only, and if the main branch on Thanon Klang Mueang is packed, there's a second branch near the Khon Kaen Hospital intersection as an option.

faq.q: About how much should I budget per person?
faq.a: Very easy on the wallet — prices run under 100 THB a bowl. Order a bowl of noodles each plus a shared plate of deep-fried taro, and you'll eat your fill of Bib Gourmand cooking for just over a hundred baht per person.

faq.q: What should I order on a first visit?
faq.a: Start with the original-recipe pink yentafo, a recipe from Yaowarat dating back to 1984. If you like it spicier, try the tom yum yentafo. Don't skip the house-made fish dumplings and fish balls, and finish with the shop's signature side, deep-fried taro.

faq.q: Where exactly is the shop, what are the hours, and when's the best time to go?
faq.a: It's on Thanon Klang Mueang, right in the center of Khon Kaen, next to the 7-Eleven in front of Villa. Open daily 07:30–24:00. The shortest queue is from breakfast through lunch, which fits nicely since MICHELIN named it one of the Best Breakfast Spots in Isan — the evening queue runs longer.
